title: Strong El Niño coincides with uneven October solar resource across South America - pv magazine Global
content:
Applications & Installations
In a new weekly update for
pv magazine
, Solcast, a DNV company, reports that solar irradiance was above average across much of the northern part of South America last month, while areas in the south-east recorded substantial deficits.
27 Nov 2026
Applications & Installations
Utility-scale
Irradiance was above average across most of South America north of 10°S in October 2026, while parts of the south-east recorded substantial deficits, according to analysis using the
Solcast API
. Global Horizontal Irradiance (GHI) was 4% above the 2007–25 average north of 10°S, but 14% below average in Paraguay, 10% below in Uruguay and 19% below in Argentina’s Pampas. Brazil’s largest distributed-solar states also recorded below average irradiance, while Chile saw below-average GHI in the centre and above-average conditions in the north and Patagonia.
El Niño typically brings drier conditions to the Amazon and northern South America and wetter conditions to the south-east. NOAA’s Oceanic Niño Index reached +2.46°C for August–October 2026, above the +2.02°C recorded in the same period in 2015 and close to the +2.59°C later peak of the 2015–16 event. October reflected this broad contrast. North of 10°S, rainfall was 11% below average and 84% of the area was sunnier than usual. GHI was 9% above average in Pernambuco, 5% above in Ceará and 4% above in Bahia.
Farther south, lower irradiance overlapped with Brazil’s largest distributed-solar markets. GHI was 19% below average in Paraná, 16% below in São Paulo, 7% below in Rio Grande do Sul and 5% below in Minas Gerais, Brazil’s four largest states for distributed solar capacity. Neighbouring countries showed a similar irradiance pattern. Paraguay was 12% wetter than average and GHI was 14% below average, while GHI was 10% below average in Uruguay and 19% below in the Argentine Pampas, despite rainfall there being below or near normal.
Wildfire smoke substantially reduced clear-sky irradiance around Manaus. Aerosol optical depth averaged 0.67, more than double the 2007–25 October average of 0.32, reducing clear-sky GHI by 7.5%. On October 18, the smokiest day, the reduction reached about onethird. However, drier conditions and reduced cloud cover largely offset the aerosol impact, leaving actual monthly GHI close to average in Manaus (+0.2%) and Porto Velho (+0.7%). Without the smoke, both cities would have experienced an unusually sunny October.
Elsewhere, drought did not necessarily bring sunnier skies. Santa Cruz, Bolivia, recorded GHI 21% below average despite drought conditions in the region. Central Chile was also cloudier, with GHI 11% below average. Santiago received 74 mm of rain in the first week of October alone, almost three times its average October total of about 26 mm. ERA5 data put rainfall for the whole month at about 174 mm, more than six times average, while GHI finished 28% below average. In contrast, GHI was 14% above average in northern Chile and 12% above in Chilean Patagonia, where weaker westerly winds and about half the usual rainfall meant fewer cloud-bearing fronts reached the Chilean side.
produces these figures by tracking clouds and aerosols at 1-2km resolution globally, using satellite data and proprietary
AI/ML algorithms
. This data is used to drive irradiance models, enabling Solcast to calculate irradiance at high resolution, with typical bias of less than 2%, and also cloud-tracking forecasts. This data is used by more than 350 companies managing over 350 GW of solar assets globally.

title: 'Rubik's Cube' molecule makes semiconductor plastic 2X more flexible
content: Researchers have developed a more flexible form of electrically conductive plastic that can stretch more than twice as far as conventional versions before cracking, potentially opening new possibilities for wearable devices and electronics designed to work inside the human body.The breakthrough, developed by researchers at the University of Toronto, uses an unusual organic molecule called bullvalene to modify the internal structure of a semiconducting plastic. The resulting material retains nearly the same electrical performance while becoming significantly more stretchable.The findings could help address a longstanding challenge in flexible electronics. Conductive plastics are increasingly being explored for applications such as flexible displays and wearable devices, but their internal crystalline structures can make them brittle under mechanical stress.Unlike conventional electronics made with rigid semiconductor materials such as silicon, flexible electronics need to bend, stretch, and conform to irregular surfaces without losing their ability to carry electrical signals.Molecule disrupts crystal structureThe research team, led by University of Toronto professor Helen Tran, investigated how bullvalene could change the structure of a conductive polymer.Bullvalene is an unusual molecule that continuously rearranges its atomic structure. Researcher Shine Huang compared its behavior to a Rubik’s Cube, with the molecule constantly shifting between different configurations.When the researchers incorporated bullvalene into a plastic semiconductor, it disrupted the material’s tightly packed crystalline arrangement. The polymer, which initially behaved like a bundle of straight wires, became more loosely organized.This structural change allowed the material to deform more easily instead of cracking under strain.Despite the disruption, the plastic maintained nearly the same electrical properties as the original material. Researchers initially expected that reducing the polymer’s crystallinity would significantly compromise its ability to conduct electricity.To understand why that did not happen, Huang examined the material at the Canadian Light Source (CLS) at the University of Saskatchewan.Using the facility’s ultrabright synchrotron light, the team investigated the modified plastic’s internal structure. The analysis revealed that crystalline regions had not disappeared. Instead, they had become considerably smaller, allowing the material to stretch while preserving pathways for electrical charge to move through it.Flexible electronics for medicineThe findings could eventually help researchers develop electronic materials that better interact with biological tissue.Rigid semiconductor materials are difficult to integrate into the human body because biological tissues are soft and constantly move. More flexible conductive materials could help address this mismatch in devices such as pacemakers, prosthetics, and other biomedical electronics.Such materials could also be useful in wearable electronics that need to maintain reliable electrical connections while bending and stretching during everyday movement.Huang is now investigating whether bullvalene could modify other types of plastics beyond conductive semiconductors. Its constantly rearranging molecular structure could potentially influence the mechanical and structural properties of a wider range of materials.Although the findings demonstrate a promising way to balance flexibility and electrical performance, further research will be needed to establish how well the material performs in practical electronic devices and whether it can be manufactured at scale.The research has been published in the journal Angewandte Chemie.

title: Elon Musk pledges more SpaceX shares for American children every year
content: Elon Musk plans to make SpaceX ownership a recurring gift for American children. The billionaire says he will donate another company share to every child in the United States each year.The pledge expands his earlier proposal to distribute two SpaceX shares to every American child. That initial giveaway carries an estimated value of $18 billion. Musk announced the additional commitment on Wednesday, shortly after SpaceX secured regulatory approval for a massive orbital computing project.The annual distribution could eventually become one of the largest recurring corporate equity giveaways. However, Musk has yet to explain how the program would work or when the first additional shares would reach recipients.Recurring share giveawayMusk’s revised proposal goes beyond a one-time transfer of company ownership. Every eligible child would receive another SpaceX share annually, potentially building a stake in the company over several years.The plan still lacks important details. Musk has not clarified how children would qualify or how families would receive the shares. He has also not explained whether recipients could sell their holdings before reaching adulthood.I will be donating another share of SpaceX to all kids in America every year— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 26, 2026SpaceX’s private status makes the proposal particularly interesting. Its shares do not trade on public stock exchanges. Their valuation instead depends on private transactions and funding activity.The financial commitment could also grow as SpaceX’s valuation changes. Each annual distribution would add another layer to the original $18 billion proposal.SpaceX eyes orbital computingThe announcement followed a significant regulatory decision involving SpaceX’s ambitions beyond satellite communications. US regulators approved the company’s plan to deploy up to 1 million satellites for data centers in space.The proposed network could move some computing infrastructure beyond Earth’s surface. However, operating data centers in orbit presents considerable engineering challenges.Computing hardware generates substantial heat, which spacecraft must dissipate without conventional cooling systems. Satellites would also need reliable power sources to support demanding workloads.Launching and maintaining such a large constellation presents another challenge. SpaceX would need to manage orbital congestion as its proposed infrastructure expands.The project reflects Musk’s growing interest in the computing industry. SpaceX could eventually provide orbital infrastructure for workloads that require enormous processing capacity.Tech philanthropy draws attentionMusk’s latest pledge arrives amid growing public scrutiny of technology billionaires. Expanding data center infrastructure has attracted criticism over electricity consumption and its environmental footprint.His philanthropic activities have largely operated through the Musk Foundation. The organization reportedly holds more than $14 billion in assets.Other technology executives have also explored large-scale equity donations. SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell and her husband previously pledged company shares for children through a Trump administration initiative.Anthropic has taken a different approach. The company committed 5% of its shares to a new fund supporting public-benefit initiatives. That commitment carried an estimated value of $54 billion at the time.Elon Musk’s proposal would put company ownership directly into children’s hands. Whether that translates into lasting financial benefits will depend on the program’s eventual structure and the future value of SpaceX.

title: Huawei targets Samsung, SK Hynix with 2X denser memory chip design
content: Huawei Technologies is exploring a new high-bandwidth memory (HBM) design that could help China reduce its dependence on foreign suppliers of a critical semiconductor component used in advanced computing systems.Researchers at the Chinese technology giant have developed an HBM architecture featuring twice the data-pin density of products currently mass-produced by South Korean chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, according to a research paper scheduled for presentation in February 2027.The development, first reported by Bloomberg, points to Huawei’s efforts to enter a memory segment dominated by Samsung, SK Hynix and US-based Micron Technology.HBM is a specialized type of memory that stacks multiple DRAM dies vertically and connects them using thousands of tiny interconnects. Its architecture allows processors to access large volumes of data at high speeds while using less physical space than conventional memory modules.The technology has become increasingly important for advanced processors powering large-scale computing workloads, where moving data quickly between memory and processing units is essential.Higher pin density boosts bandwidthThe key feature of Huawei’s reported design is its data-pin density. Doubling the density could theoretically allow more data to move between memory and processors simultaneously, significantly increasing available memory bandwidth.Higher bandwidth is particularly important for advanced computing accelerators, which require rapid access to large datasets during processing. Memory bottlenecks can limit the performance of even powerful processors, making HBM a critical part of modern semiconductor systems.However, the reported design should not be confused with a commercially ready memory product. It remains unclear how far Huawei has progressed toward manufacturing the technology or whether it can translate the proposed architecture into a working chip.Researchers frequently present theoretical chip designs at technical conferences to share new approaches and demonstrate potential improvements. Huawei is expected to present its findings at the International Solid-State Circuits Conference (ISSCC) in San Francisco in February 2027.China seeks domestic memory productionThe development comes as Chinese semiconductor companies attempt to build domestic alternatives to technologies restricted by US export controls.Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron are barred from supplying HBM to Chinese customers under US restrictions. This has created a significant challenge for domestic chipmakers seeking to manufacture advanced processors and computing systems without relying on foreign memory supplies.Huawei has already become a major domestic supplier of computing accelerators following restrictions on shipments of advanced Nvidia processors to China. It has also been expanding its semiconductor development efforts to support the country’s growing demand for computing capacity.Developing domestic HBM could address one of the industry’s most significant hardware bottlenecks. However, manufacturing advanced memory requires more than a promising circuit design. Companies must also overcome challenges involving semiconductor fabrication, vertical stacking, thermal management, interconnects, and production yields.China’s memory industry is pursuing other approaches as well. Domestic manufacturer ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) has been working on a 4F² memory architecture, which aims to increase memory density by reducing the area occupied by individual memory cells.Huawei’s reported HBM research adds another approach to China’s efforts to close the technology gap with established semiconductor manufacturers.Whether the new architecture can deliver its theoretical bandwidth gains at commercial scale remains to be seen. Its February presentation should provide a closer look at the company’s proposed design and its potential role in China’s domestic semiconductor ecosystem.

title: Physicist uses 400M GPT-6 Astra tokens to derive black hole entropy
content: Gravity is one of the fundamental forces of nature, but scientists still struggle to explain how it works at the smallest scales. A new proposal from OpenAI physicist Venkatesa Chandrasekaran offers another mathematical approach to solving that problem.His research explores how gravity behaves in four-dimensional spacetime without introducing matter. The framework also reproduces the famous formula describing black hole entropy. It recovers Einstein’s equations at low energies and includes the first quantum correction.The work has attracted attention partly because of Chandrasekaran’s collaboration with OpenAI’s models. CEO Sam Altman also praised the physicist for pursuing difficult scientific questions that others might consider impossible.Different approach to gravityChandrasekaran’s approach starts with something familiar: light. His framework studies how light travels along intersecting boundaries surrounding a region of spacetime. Physicists call this enclosed region a causal diamond.But why use light to study gravity? General relativity describes how massive objects bend spacetime. Quantum mechanics explains how nature behaves at extremely small scales. Scientists have struggled for decades to combine these two descriptions into one consistent theory.The new proposal uses the boundaries formed by light to describe gravitational behavior. Chandrasekaran then applies mathematical methods to turn that description into a quantum theory.In simpler terms, he is trying to describe gravity using the rules of quantum mechanics without assuming that spacetime itself remains fixed. The framework also produces a mathematical tool called a path integral, which helps physicists calculate the possible outcomes of a quantum system.Black hole formula emergesOne of the paper’s most important results involves black holes. According to the Bekenstein-Hawking formula, a black hole’s entropy depends on the surface area of its event horizon. Entropy broadly describes how much information about a system remains hidden from an outside observer.Chandrasekaran derives this relationship from his framework. He also calculates an additional logarithmic correction for large Schwarzschild black holes. The result matches a coefficient previously obtained by physicist Ashoke Sen using a different mathematical approach.OpenAI CEO Sam Altman commented on the research. He recalled how Chandrasekaran had believed early models could help tackle difficult mathematical problems, including Millennium Prize problems.Ven was one of the earliest believers that we could use our then-current model to solve millenium prize problems.There are a lot of brilliant people in the world, but being brilliant and also having correctly-placed confidence and courage to keep pushing on something that… https://t.co/ryBs1OX2gy— Sam Altman (@sama) November 26, 2026The framework also reproduces Einstein’s equations when applied to low-energy conditions. Importantly, Chandrasekaran includes the first quantum correction in this calculation. This suggests that the proposal can recover familiar gravitational physics while accounting for quantum effects.The collaboration also involved an extraordinary amount of computational work. Chandrasekaran says he used approximately 400 million tokens with GPT-6 Astra over several months while developing the research. The model helped with mathematical calculations and proofs, making the project an interesting example of how advanced language models are entering highly specialized scientific research.Testing the theory remainsDespite its mathematical results, the proposal still faces significant hurdles. The current framework describes gravity in a vacuum, meaning it does not include matter. It therefore does not yet provide a complete description of gravity throughout the universe.There is also a bigger question: Can the theory predict something scientists can actually measure?Recovering results that existing physics already explains is important. However, a new theory of gravity must eventually offer predictions that distinguish it from competing approaches. Without those predictions, researchers cannot determine whether it describes nature more accurately.The paper remains a preprint and still requires independent scrutiny. Its mathematical findings will need further examination by the wider physics community.

title: Fresh 215-foot reservoir boosts US' plans to pump crude through 2037
content: A U.S. energy powerhouse has recently found a 215-foot (65.4-meter) hydrocarbon reservoir off the coast of Angola, as part of a broader push to extend offshore oil production through 2037.The discovery was made by Texas-based natural gas company ExxonMobil at the Tchihumba West-01ST1 exploration well in Block 15, approximately 90 miles (145 kilometers) off Angola’s northern coast. It marks the 21st hydrocarbon discovery within the block and the second in 2026.Angola’s National Oil, Gas and Biofuels Agency (ANPG) confirmed the presence of the hydrocarbon reservoir on November 19. It moreover announced the approval of a USD 4 billion investment to revitalize two existing offshore fields and develop a third.The projects are expected to tap into additional hydrocarbon reserves and sustain production in Block 15. Its production-sharing agreement are in effect until 2037.A deepwater discoveryLocated around 217 miles (350 kilometers) northwest of Angola’s capital, Luanda, the Tchihumba West-01ST1 exploration well was reportedly drilled by the Valaris DS-9 drillship at a water depth of 4,600 feet (1,400 meters). Previously known as Ensco DS-9, the Valaris DS-9 is a sixth-generation drillship rated for water depths of up to 12,000 feet.According to ANPG, the drilling operations found a 215-foot (65.4-meter) sandy reservoir containing hydrocarbons. It has favorable physical properties for storing oil and natural gas and enabling their flow, including porosity and permeability. The Valaris DS-9 drillship.Credit: ExxonMobilThese properties determine how much oil and natural gas rocks can hold as well as how easily these fluids can move through them. While ANPG did not disclose the estimated volume of recoverable hydrocarbons, it believes the find proves the significant resource potential that remains within Block 15.“The formalization of the Final Investment Decision for the redevelopment of Kizomba A and B, associated with the new discovery of hydrocarbons at the Tchihumba West-01ST1 well, represents an important milestone for the national oil industry and attests to the exploratory potential still existing in mature producing fields in Angola,” Paulino Jerónimo, ANPG board chairman, shared. Extending field lifeAt the same time, ExxonMobil and its partners finalized their investment decision for three offshore fields. The plans include redeveloping the existing Kizomba A and Kizomba B fields, and developing the Likembe field.According to ANPG officials, the decision followed the approval of the Kizomba C redevelopment in 2025. It also concluded the investment approval process for the Block 15 Life Extension Project.The initiative is expected to use existing offshore facilities to access and develop additional oil and gas resources in the Kizomba area. Brian Unietis, ExxonMobil’s general director, said that the two milestones demonstrate the strength of Block 15 and its potential for further development. He noted that investment, technology and exploration remain key to identifying new opportunities. “With the support of the extension of the production sharing agreement for Block 15 until 2037 and approximately USD 4 billion in planned new investments, including the development of the Likembe field and the activities of the Block 15 Life Extension project, we are well positioned to continue generating value for Angola, our partners and our shareholders,” Unietis stated in a press release.

title: 聚力蓝海，破局共生｜2026 第四届海上光伏大会将于12月举办-索比光伏网
content:
在 “双碳” 目标与 “海洋强国” 战略持续驱动下，海上光伏产业正加速从技术探索阶段迈向规模化开发新阶段。依托不占用陆地资源、发电出力相对稳定的突出优势，海上光伏成为沿海地区新能源布局的重要方向。其中，风光同场开发模式可复用现有海上风电送出、海域配套设施，有效压缩用海成本，协同提升海域利用效率，被行业视作极具发展潜力的技术路线，国内多个沿海省份已启动大规模规划布局，蓝海开发持续提速。
快速扩张的背后，海上光伏产业仍面临多重系统性难题亟待攻克。海洋高盐雾、高湿度环境会加速光伏组件、箱变等设备腐蚀老化；台风、巨浪等极端海洋工况，对结构设计、设备抗灾能力提出更高要求，相关标准体系仍有待完善。海上作业受海况制约，有效施工窗口期短，桩基工程造价偏高、海上吊装风险突出，项目经济性短板成为规模化落地的主要瓶颈。与此同时，大规模海上光伏电力并网消纳方案、项目开发与海洋生态保护之间的平衡机制，也是产业向前推进必须妥善解决的现实课题。
为直面行业痛点、凝聚产业合力，索比光伏网联合中电工程西北电力设计院，定于 2026年12月24日举办2026第四届海上光伏大会。本次大会聚焦海上光伏全链条发展痛点，设置多重核心研讨方向，覆盖行业政策与区域规划、风光同场融合开发方案、设备海洋环境可靠性验证、并网送出与电力消纳路径、海上施工安全及降本路径、用海合规管理、海洋生态协同保护、智能运维体系建设等关键议题。
大会将汇聚业主单位、设计院、装备厂商、施工企业、科研机构等多方主体，搭建高效的技术交流、经验互通、资源对接平台，围绕共性难题开展深度研讨，分享工程实践案例、前沿技术方案与创新思路，共同探寻海上光伏规模化高质量发展的破局路径。
随着海上光伏进入规模化前夜，行业亟需统一技术共识、完善落地方案、理顺开发机制。本次大会旨在打通产业链上下游，推动技术迭代、成本优化与生态协同并行，助力海上光伏产业行稳致远，为我国海洋能源开发、清洁能源体系建设注入新动能。

title: 一串手链，如何连接起中国光伏的产业力量？-索比光伏网
content:
最近，光伏圈有一场不太一样的接力。
没有新品发布，没有商业签约，二十多位光伏女性从业者，通过一串手链、一个价值关键词、一段真实的职业故事，将自己对行业的理解、实践与思考，传递给下一位同行者。
这就是由中国绿色供应链联盟光伏专委会(ECOPV)与隆基绿能联合发起的“她力量·向光而行”中国光伏女性共创计划。
在一个习惯了用吉瓦、效率、成本和市场份额衡量发展成果的行业里，这场接力提供了一个不同的观察视角：当我们谈论中国光伏取得的成就时，那些推动行业向前的人，以及她们创造的价值，是否也应该被更多人看见?
一、中国光伏的成就，不只有技术参数
过去二十年，中国光伏创造了令人瞩目的产业奇迹。从转换效率的不断突破，到度电成本的持续下降，再到产业链的规模化发展，中国光伏成为全球能源转型的重要推动力量。
但一个产业的发展，从来不只是技术参数的不断刷新。
一块光伏组件从实验室走向千家万户，从生产制造到安装交付，再到二三十年的稳定运行，背后涉及技术研发、标准制定、生产制造、市场开拓、电站运维、资源循环等无数环节。
每一个环节的进步，都有人在推动;每一个行业难题的解决，都有人在寻找答案。
尤其是在当前的行业周期中，当技术创新、市场竞争、全球化发展和可持续发展等课题同时摆在中国光伏面前，我们更需要重新认识推动产业向前的多元力量。
这也是“她力量·向光而行”发起的初衷之一：从一个个真实的人出发，记录那些正在发生的产业创新与价值创造，寻找中国光伏持续向前的力量。
二、她们，为中国光伏做成了什么?
在这场接力中，一个比“女性如何在行业中坚持”更值得关注的问题逐渐浮现：这些女性，究竟为中国光伏创造了什么价值?
让中国光伏拥有更多国际话语权。
国际能源署IEA PVPS副主席、Task 1和Task 12中国代表、中国绿色供应链联盟光伏专委会秘书长吕芳，长期推动光伏组件绿色设计、回收处理和碳足迹标准的国际化对接。
从技术领先到参与国际规则制定，中国光伏的全球竞争力不仅体现在产品走向世界，也体现在中国的技术实践、产业经验和发展理念能够被世界理解与认可。
让光伏的绿色价值延续至全生命周期。
河南永安光循环保科技有限公司董事长周瑾，从实验室走向产线，推动退役光伏组件回收的产业化落地，让废弃组件中的玻璃、铝、银、铜和硅材料重新进入资源循环。
当今天安装的光伏组件在未来陆续进入退役阶段，如何实现资源的高效回收与再利用，将成为产业可持续发展必须回答的问题。而她和团队，正在提前寻找答案。
让每一座光伏电站发好每一度电。
国家电投集团黄河公司新能源集控中心集团光伏专业首席技师李翠婷，在青海高原深耕光伏运维14年，牵头构建企业级新能源智慧集控技术体系，支撑国内814座光伏场站提质增效。
从高原上的一座座电站，到可复制、可推广的智慧运维体系，她将长期积累的一线经验转化为产业能力，让光伏电站的长期发电价值得到更好的保障。
让绿色能源更好地融入百姓生活。
创维光伏高级结构工程师庞红蕾，从农村居民的实际生活需求出发，将光伏屋顶与建筑安全、空间利用和美学设计相结合，推动“小阳楼”走进更多家庭。
光伏不只是一套发电设备，也可以成为改善生活空间的一部分。从技术思维走向用户思维，这同样是产品创新的重要方向。
让制造创新发生在每一个细节。
山西又川新能源有限公司董事长、总经理许聪，带领团队深耕光伏边框领域，推动新材料、新工艺在组件边框上的应用，在结构强度与全生命周期减碳方面探索新的解决方案。
边框只是光伏组件的一个部件，但正是产业链上一个个细分领域的持续创新，共同支撑起中国光伏的制造竞争力。
从国际标准到资源循环，从电站运维到产品设计，再到制造创新，她们身处不同的产业环节，却在回答同一个问题：
如何让中国光伏发展得更好?
她们不是产业发展的旁观者，也不只是行业故事中的一个特殊群体，而是中国光伏产业的建设者、创新者和推动者。
三、从一个人的价值，到一群人的力量
“她力量·向光而行”的起点，是一串手链。
隆基绿能分布式业务中国区总裁牛燕燕曾亲手制作手链，送给光伏行业的女性同行者。一颗颗珠子被串在一起，也让一个想法逐渐形成：能否以这样一种方式，把来自不同企业、不同岗位、不同产业环节的优秀女性连接起来，让她们的故事和价值被更多人看见?
牛燕燕长期扎根光伏市场一线，从市场开拓、渠道建设到推动产品创新，带领团队不断探索如何为客户创造更大的价值。
吕芳则长期致力于产业协同、国际交流和绿色发展，也通过秀洲光伏女性精英联盟等平台，持续关注和推动光伏女性的交流与成长。
两位发起者有着不同的职业经历，却有着共同的期待：让更多光伏女性走到镜头前，讲述自己做过的事、解决过的问题，以及为行业创造的价值。
于是，一串手链成为连接的信物，一个价值关键词成为每个人职业实践的注脚，一段真实故事成为产业发展的记录。
连接、长期、共创、专业、责任、创新……
每一个关键词背后，都有一段具体的职业经历;每一次接力，都让另一位同行者的价值被发现。
当这些关键词不断汇聚，它们也将成为观察中国光伏产业发展的一份独特样本。
四、因为同行，所以更有力量
今天的中国光伏，仍然面临着诸多挑战。技术需要继续突破，市场需要持续开拓，产业链需要不断完善，全球能源转型也需要更多创新与合作。
面对这些共同的课题，每一个光伏人都在以自己的方式寻找答案。
有人在实验室里突破技术边界，有人在生产线上打磨制造工艺，有人在市场一线解决客户难题，有人在国际舞台上推动产业交流，也有人在高原、乡村和工业园区，守护着一座座光伏电站的稳定运行。
这些力量不尽相同，却共同构成了中国光伏持续向前的动力。
“她力量·向光而行”希望做的，正是记录这些力量、连接这些力量、传递这些力量。
它从光伏女性的故事出发，但最终希望带给每一位光伏从业者更多启发：在行业发展的不同阶段，我们能够创造什么价值?又能从同行者身上获得怎样的力量?
穿越周期，从来不是某一个人、某一家企业的独自前行，而是无数产业同行者在各自的领域持续创造价值，共同推动行业向前。
五、接力仍在继续
从一串手链出发，“她力量·向光而行”正在连接越来越多来自不同产业环节的女性同行者。
随着接力的持续开展，更多真实故事、价值关键词和行业思考将被记录下来，逐渐汇聚成一份属于中国光伏人的“力量图谱”。
我们期待，这不仅是一份关于中国光伏女性的记录，也是一份关于中国光伏如何持续创新、共同成长、穿越周期的记录。
一颗珠子，代表一个人的价值;一串手链，连接一群人的力量。
让每一份价值被看见，让每一份力量被传递。
因为同行，所以更有力量。
“她力量·向光而行”，下一棒，期待更多精彩。
如果让你推荐下一位光伏女性同行者，你会选择谁?她又为这个行业创造了怎样的价值?欢迎在留言区分享。

title: 海上光伏！河北将推动海上清洁能源项目建设-索比光伏网
政策分类路径: 政策 > 战略规划型政策 > 规划目标
政策分类依据: 《“绿动渤海”行动方案（2026—2030年）河北篇》提出海上风电光伏项目建设的阶段目标与任务安排
content:
按照日前发布的《“绿动渤海”行动方案（2026—2030年）河北篇》，河北省将有序推进海上风电光伏项目建设，加快秦皇岛、唐山、沧州海上清洁能源项目建设，督促已批复项目加快实施。推进海上风电与海洋石油、海洋牧场、海洋算力融合发展，结合唐秦负荷中心需求探索实施“海上风电+绿电直连”项目。
渤海是河北重要的海洋能源资源战略接续区，也是“绿动渤海”绿色航运转型的清洁能源基座。行动方案将海上新能源开发纳入绿色航运转型总体框架，围绕“陆海统筹、风光并举、融合发展、安全高效”总体思路，对海上新能源开发与港航绿色低碳转型深度融合作出系统安排。
海上风电光伏规模化推进。河北省在秦皇岛、唐山、沧州沿海三市科学布局，有序推进海上风电、海上光伏项目建设。海上风电方面，山海关海上风电一期、河北建投唐山海上风电、唐山顺桓海上风电等项目梯次推进。海上光伏方面，秦皇岛市180万千瓦海上光伏示范试点项目、秦皇岛市200万千瓦“风光同场”海上光伏项目加快实施。
探索海上新能源绿电直连实现新突破。河北省将落实单用户、多用户绿电直连配套政策，建立“随报随批”绿色审批通道，结合唐山、秦皇岛负荷中心需求，指导沿海区域探索实施“海上风电+绿电直连”示范，推动海上绿电通过专用线路向钢铁、化工等临港大工业点对点供电，助力重点产品满足出口碳足迹要求，把海上绿电优势切实转化为临港产业绿色竞争优势。
探索新能源与海洋多元融合发展。有序推动海上风电、海上光伏与海洋牧场、海洋算力、海水淡化、海水制氢等集成融合，培育海洋绿色新兴产业，形成多能互补、立体开发、融合发展的海洋能源利用新格局。加快推动油田绿色发展，鼓励绿电就近接入油田生产系统，推动秦皇岛—曹妃甸油田群岸电扩容，支持秦皇岛27-3油田建成“低碳零碳作业区”。大力发展新能源船舶、高端海工装备等绿色制造产业，谋划实施秦皇岛无人船制造、智能港口设备制造等项目，有序布局海水制氢等前沿产业。
省发展改革委将按照行动方案部署，进一步加强与国家及省直有关部门沟通对接，统筹海域空间、生态保护、航运安全等多重因素，有序推进海上新能源项目前期工作与工程建设，积极谋划储备后续项目，持续扩大海上清洁能源供给，为绿色航运、港口运营和临港产业提供稳定清洁电力保障。

title: 海上风电与海上光伏融合发展研究进展与未来挑战-索比光伏网
政策分类路径: 政策 > 战略规划型政策 > 产业方向
政策分类依据: 文中回顾国家推动海洋能源融合开发的系列政策指导意见，确定海上风光融合发展的重点技术方向
content:
海上风电的大规模开发和有效利用是提升国家能源安全、助力“双碳”目标实现的重要途径。自2021年起，我国海上风电新增装机容量和装机总量居世界第一。随着近海开发资源的饱和及平价时代的到来，海上风电逐渐向深远海方向发展，为了提高资源的利用率、降低开发成本，海上风电融合发展成为大势所趋。海上风能资源和太阳能资源丰富，风电和光伏的出力特性不同，具有一定的互补性，可以融合发展，但目前，海洋环境复杂、海上光伏发电不稳定、造价成本高、易受风浪破坏。
近年来，国家为推动海洋能源的融合开发发布了系列政策支持。2024年，自然资源部《自然资源要素支撑产业高质量发展指导目录（2024年本）》指出，海上光伏可在省管海域内围海养殖区、海上风电场区、电厂确权温排水区、长期闲置或废弃盐田等4类已开发建设海域选址，这为海上风电与海上光伏的融合发展提供了重要政策支撑。2025年，自然资源部等六部委联合印发《关于推动海洋能规模化利用的指导意见》，明确指出“促进海洋能新技术、新模式发展，推动海洋能与各类海上生产活动融合发展”“积极构建安全可靠的海上新型能源体系”。海上风电与海上光伏融合开发可将单位海域的能源产出密度和经济效益最大化，同时集约共享输电、运维等基础设施与海洋使用权，极大降低了开发成本与生态足迹，是突破单一能源时空局限性、实现海洋空间立体化利用的革命性突破。
本文旨在回顾海上风电、海上光伏及海上“风光同场”发展历程，梳理海上风光融合发展现状，根据海上风电与海上光伏的成果，从电力融合输出、结构可靠度与成本、协同运维等方面提出困难与挑战，为海上风电与海上光伏规模化融合开发提供参考。
海上风电与海上光伏融合现状
全球海上光伏尚处于起步阶段，开工项目数量较少且多为示范验证性项目。影响其商业化开发的主要因素包括：海域使用审批严格、建设成本居高不下、能源供应不稳定、海上专用光伏组件性能有待提高等。“风光同场”是目前解决上述问题、推进海上光伏商业化进程的最有效途径之一。国外海上风光融合发展概念虽较早被提出，但对应支持政策明显不足。2019年11月，欧盟委员会发布了《欧洲绿色协议》，为了响应该协议，荷兰政府采取了更加积极的、支持性的监管方法，通过一站式服务模式降低开发商风险，促进海上风电的成本下降和规模化发展。2024年8月，欧盟委员会能源总局（DGENER）正在准备关于在海上可再生能源招标中纳入非价格标准的详细建议，预计将于2025年发布，将涵盖多源海上能源园区，其中波浪、漂浮式光伏能源园区被整合到海上风电场中，并支持成员国在其国家海洋空间规划（MSP）中包含多用途区域。
2021年11月，国家能源局和科学技术部联合发布《“十四五”能源领域科技创新规划》（国能发科技〔2021〕58号），提出开展近海漂浮式光伏系统技术及高可靠性组件、部件技术研究。2021年12月，国家发展和改革委员会印发《江苏沿海地区发展规划（2021－2025年）》（发改地区〔2021〕1862号），规划明确指出：支持探索海上风电、光伏发电和海洋牧场融合发展。2022年10月，国家能源局发布《能源碳达峰碳中和标准化提升行动计划》，提出依托大型风电光伏基地建设海上风电基地和海上光伏项目建设，设立标准化示范工程。2023年3月，山东省能源局印发《山东省能源绿色低碳高质量发展三年行动计划（20232025年）》鲁能源规划〔2023〕29号的通知，通知指出：探索“风光同场”海上清洁能源开发模式，2025年，风电和光伏发电装机分别达到25吉瓦和57吉瓦以上。2024年8月，上海市发展和改革委员会印发《上海市“风光同场”海上光伏开发建设方案》（沪发改能源〔2024〕177号），明确在同一海域协同布局海上风电和光伏项目，提高海域利用效率。2024年启动首轮1吉瓦海上光伏项目竞争配置，2025年继续推进剩余项目开发，并要求配套储能不低于光伏装机容量的20%。2025年2月，国家能源局与国家发展和改革委员会联合发布的《关于深化新能源上网电价市场化改革促进新能源高质量发展的通知》（发改价格〔2025〕136号）中明确指出：光伏、风电、生物质等新能源上网电量全部进入电力市场；设立“新能源可持续发展价格结算机制”，在市场外对纳入机制的电量进行差价补偿或回收；明确禁止地方政府将储能配置作为项目核准、并网的前置条件。山东省、上海市等地率先实施，2025年8月，上海市发展和改革委员会、山东省发展和改革委员会分别发布《关于上海市贯彻落实新能源上网电价市场化改革有关事项的通知》《山东省新能源上网电价市场化改革实施方案》（鲁发改价格〔2025〕576号）。
为应对全球气候变化、推动能源结构转型，海上可再生能源的开发利用正从单一风电向“风光储氢”多能融合模式加速演进，由于海上风光融合具有资源互补属性显著，荷兰、意大利等欧洲国家率先于2010年前后进行探索。2019年12月，荷兰Oceans of Energy公司在北海部署了世界上第一个离岸型海上光伏系统，该系统经受住了10～13米海浪、超过100公里/小时的强台风侵袭，也为Hollandse Kust Noord项目奠定了技术基础。2023年，荷兰在Hollandse Kust Noord海上风电场中启动“海上风电+海上光伏+电池储能+绿色制氢”超级混合体建设，项目离岸185公里，共安装69台11兆瓦海上风电机组，已于2023年并网发电，如下图所示：

● 时间发展历程
早期风力发电多集中在欧洲。1887年，英国科学家詹姆斯·布莱思制造了人类第一台风力发电机。20世纪初，丹麦建成了风力发电集群，为海上风电的发展奠定了基础。海上风电发展历程可追溯至20世纪70年代，多集中于丹麦、瑞典、荷兰和英国等欧洲国家，可分为技术可行性验证、商业化开发、规模化及深远海开发3个阶段。经过数十年的技术探索，从1990年瑞典建成的世界首台海上风电机组，到1991年丹麦风电企业建成了全球第一座海上风电场Vindeby，再到2001年期间，丹麦、荷兰、英国等国家合计建设了9个海上风电项目，其中5个项目容量低于10兆瓦，但充分验证了海上风电的技术可行性。从2002－2011年，世界海上风电的发展仍以欧洲为重点，政府扶持下，海上风电建设逐步实现商业化开发并规模化发展。2012年至今，欧洲率先开展深远海风电技术探索，并于2009－2017年间建成全球首个商业化漂浮式海上风电场Hywind Scotland，标志着海上风电向深远海迈进的关键突破。与此同时，随着全球对新能源需求的快速增长，发展海上风电的国家持续增加，以中国为代表的亚洲国家加速布局，在装机规模与技术创新方面迅速赶超欧洲，推动全球海上风电产业进入新一轮高质量发展期。
我国海上风电虽起步较晚，但得益于政策的大力支持、技术不断创新、产业链不断完善等，已迅速成长为全球最大的海上风电市场。我国海上风电可分为前期探索、示范试验、小规模开发、规模化快速发展、高质量发展5个阶段。2007年11月8日，中国首台海上风电机组在渤海绥中油田建成发电，标志着我国海上风电探索取得实质性突破，也拉开了我国海上风电开发的序幕。2008－2010年，龙源如东海上（潮间带）试验风电场和上海东海大桥100兆瓦海上风电示范项目的相继批复，标志着我国进入了示范项目建设阶段。2011－2015年，由于成本等多方面因素影响，海上风电发展较为缓慢，项目主要集中在潮间带地区。2016－2021年底，前期技术储备、愈加完善的产业链、补贴政策的支持、更加透明的投融资环境使我国海上风电进入快速发展的阶段。2022年至今，随着补贴政策的退坡、近海开发资源的饱和，海上风电逐渐向集约化、高质量发展转型。

● 结构体系研发
自21世纪初漂浮式海上光伏技术理念萌芽以来，全球科研机构与企业已开展了长期的技术攻关与工程验证，逐步发展出适应不同海况条件的多样化结构型式，如下图所示。目前可分为固定式和漂浮式两大类。固定式海上光伏通过桩基和支架将光伏阵列稳固于近海或潮间带，适合水位较浅、风浪较小的区域，其结构稳固、发电效率高且便于维护，但受水深和地质条件限制，适用范围较窄；漂浮式海上光伏主要采用浮体结构和支架支撑光伏板，可布设于深水海域，但浮体抗风浪设计复杂、成本较高。不同海上光伏结构特点对比如下表所示。

海上光伏系统需依靠支架结构将光伏组件支撑于海平面以上，固定式与漂浮式海上光伏的支架形式存在显著差异：漂浮式支架下部与浮体相连，光伏组件通过安装于浮体上方的支架实现稳定布置；固定式支架下部固定于桩基础，上部支撑光伏组件。
固定式较漂浮式海上光伏技术更为成熟，常见固定式光伏支架有桁架式和柔性支架式等结构，如下图所示。其中，桁架式支架为刚性结构，可承受较大的风浪荷载，无需复杂的张拉和调整工序，施工过程相对简单，维护和检修成本较低，但需要较多的钢材来保证结构的强度和稳定性，导致成本较高。柔性支架式采用张拉索结构，可有效分散风荷载进而提高抗风能力，相较于桁架式用钢量少且成本低，但柔性支架在风浪荷载作用下易产生振动和变形，需定期检查和维护拉索结构保持其张力和稳定性，且对设计和施工要求高。
↑ 固定式海上光伏支架分类
现阶段固定式海上光伏主要采用桩基支架式方案，技术较为成熟，但随着水深增加环境更为复杂导致成本急剧增加，目前已在国华山东垦利1吉瓦等多个项目中应用，每个支架平台平面尺寸34米×60米，综合考虑防腐蚀、抗风浪、抗浮冰、抗浪潮、抗洋流、防碰撞等多因素，桩基础采用Q355D钢管桩。柔性支架在海上光伏的应用处于探索阶段，其大跨度、高净空的特点使其在近海滩涂区域具有一定的优势，可有效节约成本、缩短施工周期，已在大唐诏安西山100兆瓦渔光互补光伏电站项目应用，但对于深远海台风多发区海域仍需进一步验证。
此外，数字化与运维亦是海上光伏项目开发建设的重点，以国内某吉瓦级海上光伏项目为例，该项目采用“集中监控、无人值班、少人值守”的管理目标，进行智慧化建设方案设计，接入项目新能源安全生产监控平台所需的数据采集与传输、网络基础。运维采用200吨级运维母船配备1－2艘自带动力式运维工作筏，运维母船航行于光伏场区边界之间的50米宽通道内，当光伏场区内需要进行日常检修和维护工作时，由运维母船携带检修人员及设备，在场区边界通道行驶至运维区域周边，抵近后经自带动力的运维工作筏靠近组件大平台，工作筏靠平台后人员登平台进行运维检修工作。
融合发展关键技术挑战
● 电力系统输出
风力发电与太阳能发电存在显著的差异，风力发电波动性大、低同时率且平均出力较低，风速变化使得风力发电具有随机性且无明显昼夜规律，不同海上风电场的风速变化并不同步，总出力的“抵消效应”使整体波动幅度小于单个风电场，但若集中在同一海域的风电场，总出力波动幅度会显著增大。而光伏发电具有昼夜间歇性、高同时率和平均出力略高的特性，显著的昼夜规律且同一气候带的天气变化会使得相同场区光伏出力同步下降，同时率通常保持较高水平。
因此，不同的出力特性需配套储能或智能调度系统以实现稳定并网，但目前仍存在多方面技术困境：（1）海上风电和海上光伏的出力预测难度大，需借助高精度气象模型和实时监测技术，而海上环境复杂、监测数据不足、季节性天气系统不确定等多方面因素致使现有技术的精度和可靠性仍面临挑战，若预测偏差大将引起储能或调度系统“反应不及”，导致电网频率不稳；（2）储能配置复杂，风光融合发电出力互补性有限，使得储能需同时平抑短时波动和应对长时缺电，长时储能需采用氢储能或压缩空气储能，高盐雾、潮湿、台风等环境因素影响储能和电力电子器件（如变流器）寿命，故障率攀升；（3）风光同场融合设计时设备接口、通信协议尚无成熟标准可借鉴参考。
● 耐久性与成本协同
固定式海上光伏系统通常适用于水深15米以内的海域，在此范围内，其结构稳定性和经济性相对可控。然而，随着水深增加，基础结构用量和施工难度将呈指数级增长，导致建设成本显著增加，主要原因为深水区需更长的桩基础、更高耐久性的支撑结构以及大型施工设备投入。漂浮式海上光伏虽可突破水深限制，但其面临的技术瓶颈更为突出，主要包括：复杂的锚固系统、动态环境下的电力传输、波浪作用下的组件稳定性等。上述技术挑战使得漂浮式光伏单位造价居高不下，加之缺乏成熟的商业运营案例，导致该技术在未来5-10年内难以实现规模化应用。
固定式光伏系统在台风等极端工况下需承受巨大的风载荷、波浪引起的持续动力冲击，需对支撑结构进行超常加固，导致用钢量大幅增加，直接推高整体建设成本。漂浮式海上光伏系统虽可通过柔性结构消解部分波浪能量，但其在极端工况下的系统完整性、组件防水性以及锚泊系统可靠性等方面仍存在重大技术隐患；特别是在盐雾腐蚀、海洋生物附着等长期环境因素叠加作用下，任何设计缺陷都可能导致灾难性后果，多因素影响使得当下漂浮式海上光伏难以满足商业化运营的可靠性要求。
● 抗台风设计规范
中国沿海作为全球台风灾害最频发的海域之一，90%以上的海上风电场都曾遭受过强台风袭击，无论是在已建还是拟建海上风电场中建设海上光伏场，海上光伏设施均面临极其严苛的环境考验。台风往往伴随着极端风速和巨大波浪，其对结构基础产生巨大的冲击力和周期性疲劳载荷。现有的风机基础结构设计在面对超过设计标准的极端台风时，可能显露出不足，存在发生动力灾变的风险。
我国海上风电设计标准最初参考欧洲规范，但我国东南沿海独特的“强台风-软弱土”地质条件使得欧洲标准不完全适用。此外，行业内的“低价竞争”可能导致部分项目在关键材料、结构强度或抗风等级上未能留有足够的安全裕量，牺牲了长期可靠性。海上光伏作为较新的领域，专门的抗台风设计规范、标准尚不完善，海上项目多参考陆上或近海经验，但深远海的风浪联合作用条件更为严苛，且台风带来的风载荷可能远超现有设计预期，易导致组件损坏或漂浮式电站失稳。
固定式基础的海上风电与光伏协同运维面临着空间冲突与作业效率的挑战。由于单桩、导管架等海上风电基础通常占据海域核心位置，光伏板只能以环绕或间隔方式布置，风光同场密集布局导致运维船舶的接近路径受限，尤其在风机塔筒周围形成作业盲区。此外，风机定期检修与光伏组件清洁维护无法同步进行，两者分步作业不仅延长了运维工期，还使原本受海况严格限制的作业窗口期进一步被压缩。再者，光伏系统的汇流箱、逆变器等电气设备对盐雾腐蚀更为敏感，其腐蚀速率比风电设备更快，需制定差异化的防腐维护策略，包括更频繁的绝缘检测和密封件更换。
漂浮式基础的海上风光协同系统则面临更为复杂的动态环境运维难题。漂浮式平台的六自由度运动，特别是垂荡和纵摇运动会导致光伏阵列发生非均匀位移，长期累积可能引发支架结构疲劳甚至连接件失效，而风机系泊系统的系泊力变化可能进一步加剧干扰。此外，光伏阵列与风机动态电缆之间的相对运动使得水下电缆存在缠绕风险，常规巡检必须依赖潜水员或水下机器人协同作业，单次检修成本可达固定式基础的2～3倍。漂浮式光伏的年故障率比固定式光伏高，且随着运营时间延长，锚链松弛与浮体腐蚀等耦合问题可能引发连锁故障。当前漂浮式风光一体化系统缺乏超过5年以上的长期运行数据，其稳定性与可靠性仍存在较大不确定性，给运维计划的制定带来了额外挑战。

title: 海尔新能源亮相
content:
11月25日至27日，由国家能源局、山东省人民政府联合主办的第四届“一带一路”能源部长会议在青岛举办，2026国际能源技术装备展览会同期举行。国家能源局、山东省人民政府有关领导、80多个国家的能源部长、驻华使节和高级别代表，国际组织负责人及中外企业、研究机构等参会，同时200余家能源装备企业集中参展。在这一高规格国际合作平台上，海尔新能源携AI赋能的家庭、工商业微电网和AIDC算电协同解决方案亮相，同步展示AI能源机器人、智能微网储能一体机、AI光伏逆变器、AI混合逆变器、集装箱大储、UPS等产品，并受到多国代表的好评。
国家发展改革委等四部门印发的《关于推进共建“一带一路”绿色发展的意见》提到，2030年共建“一带一路”绿色发展格局基本形成，“走出去”企业绿色发展能力显著增强。紧扣绿色高质量共建“一带一路”与能源转型方向，海尔新能源搭建“纳晖”能源互联网生态平台，以 “云‑边‑端” 协同的垂域大模型为底座，智能体矩阵协同，形成了覆盖家庭一体化、工商业能碳一体化、AIDC算电协同智慧能源解决方案方案矩阵，与中外参会伙伴交流各类场景解决方案。
展会上，围绕家庭、工商业、智算中心三类典型用能场景，海尔新能源定制“发、储、管、售、用”全流程解决方案，并完成从感知、决策到调度的AI+新能源闭环。家庭一体化场景中，家庭AI能源机器人可智能感知用电习惯，预测供需与电价，兼顾备电可靠与用能经济，适配家庭、社区等多元场景；工商业能碳一体化场景中，统筹工商业通用AI能源机器人、智慧能源管理平台并依托自研AI储能、逆变器产品矩阵形成统一主体，实现节能降本、智慧运营与资产增值；AIDC算电协同方案里，通过算力与电力协同，实现绿电稳定服务算力需求，提供AIDC绿电直连与供备电一体化解决方案、AIDC算电冷一体化解决方案；通过能源与算力生态协同，把AI融入业务全流程、全场景，并运用生态运营思维协同多方生态伙伴，建设分布式边缘侧AI数据中心赛道。
会议期间，国家能源局相关领导及外方能源部长、驻华使节等与会嘉宾一行参观海尔新能源展台，对海尔新能源以AI科技赋能的智慧能源方案及应用实践给予肯定，认为该方案贴合“一带一路”国家能源转型的实际需求，具有良好示范价值。目前，海尔新能源的产品与方案已覆盖全球70多个国家和地区，并形成可复制的本土化合作模式。

title: 国家能源局四川监管办公室原党组成员张毅接受纪律审查和监察调查-索比光伏网
content:
国家能源局四川监管办公室原党组成员、一级调研员张毅涉嫌严重违纪违法，目前正接受中央纪委国家监委驻国家发展改革委纪检监察组纪律审查和四川省攀枝花市监委监察调查。
张毅，男，汉族，1971年2月生，四川西昌人，在职研究生学历。1994年7月参加工作，2008年6月加入中国共产党。
1994年7月至2003年1月，先后在四川宜宾国际经济贸易发展中心、成都市锦江区老年活动中心、四川省紫坪铺开发有限责任公司工作；
2003年1月至2009年7月，历任四川省紫坪铺开发有限责任公司综合服务中心副主任，国家电监会成都监管办公室供电监管处副处长；
2009年7月至2026年10月，历任国家电监会成都监管办公室供电监管处处长，国家电监会四川省电力监管专员办公室输供电监管处处长，国家能源局四川监管办公室行业监管处处长，稽查处处长，党组成员、稽查处处长，党组成员、综合处处长，党组成员、综合处处长、一级调研员，党组成员、一级调研员；
2026年10月至今，国家能源局四川监管办公室干部。

title: 西北—华东绿电联合交易启动会在北京召开-索比光伏网
政策分类路径: 政策 > 监管落实型政策 > 市场势力
政策分类依据: 西北—华东绿电联合交易通过'一次报价、联合交易'机制规范跨省跨区绿电市场交易规则，属于落实全国统一电力市场的市场接入与交易机制设计
content:
11月26日，西北—华东绿电联合交易启动会在北京召开，国家能源局党组成员、副局长宋宏坤出席会议并讲话，宣布西北—华东绿电联合交易正式启动，国家电网公司总经理张文峰出席会议。
会议指出，西北—华东绿电联合交易是贯彻落实国办发〔2026〕4号文件的重要任务，也是全国统一电力市场体系建设取得的又一项重要标志性成果。“一次报价、联合交易”以西北—华东
绿电起步，经营主体通过一次申报量价曲线，同步形成跨省跨区、省内成交结果，架起两个区域之间
绿电桥梁”。联合交易既立足特高压直流通道物理联络条件，也兼顾两地资源禀赋互补的现实需求；既为西北开辟新能源消纳新出口，也为华东电力用户提供更多绿电选择。
会议强调，西北—华东绿电联合交易要统筹把握好“进”的方向与“稳”的要求
，必须精心组织、周密实施。要坚持底线思维，密切跟踪交易组织和电网运行情况，加强全流程监管；要坚持系统观念，做好跨省跨区与省内交易规则衔接、运营时序协同和平台互联互通，优化市场设计；要坚持循序渐进，稳步扩大参与范围，推动联合交易常态化运营，为完善全国统一电力市场体系积累有益经验。
首次联合交易共有1615家经营主体参与申报，
包括新能源企业1188家，用户侧主体427家，覆盖上海、江苏、浙江、安徽、福建、陕西、甘肃、青海、宁夏、新疆十省（区、市）。交易出清电量61.7亿千瓦时，其中跨省跨区绿电19.5亿千瓦时，省内绿电42.2亿千瓦时，平均交易价格0.204元/千瓦时。
国家发展改革委、国家能源局有关司及派出机构负责同志，相关政府主管部门负责同志，有关电网企业、发电企业、售电公司、电力用户等经营主体代表参加会议。

title: Windcat expands fleet with second MP-ASV order from Damen
content:
Windcat has signed a contract with Damen Shipyards Group for a second Multi-Purpose
Accommodation Support Vessel (MP-ASV) in its innovation series.
The agreement reinforces the companies' long-term relationship following
the delivery of the first vessel and includes an option for five additional
vessels.
According to the companies, the MP-ASV is a new type of vessel designed
to support operations across the offshore wind industry. Damen said the
design draws on its experience in the design and construction of commissioning
service operation vessels (CSOVs).
The MP-ASV features a 102 metre by 20 metre hull and 720 square metres
of deck space, with accommodation for up to 190 people on board. The vessel
is also equipped with a 150 tonne subsea crane and can be fitted with remotely
operated vehicles (ROVs), enabling it to support a wide range of offshore
wind activities.
The vessels have been designed with efficiency in mind, featuring a battery
system that enables peak shaving, spinning reserve and electric sailing.
They are also equipped with a dual-fuel hydrogen auxiliary generator, providing
additional low-emission operating options.
Damen Sales Director Joost van der Weiden said: "With the Innovation
Series, we have jointly developed a vessel that will further enhance Windcat's
capabilities to support its clients in the offshore energy industry in
the years ahead."
Windcat Managing Director Willem van der Wel said: "By combining the
capabilities of a multi-purpose support vessel with high-quality offshore
accommodation, we are creating a versatile solution that responds to the
evolving needs of our customers.
"Building on our successful collaboration with Damen, this additional
order marks another important step in developing a future-ready fleet,
with a strong focus on operational flexibility, efficiency and decarbonisation."

title: Baltic Wind selects Elecsys Technologies to support operations and maintenance
content:
Baltic Wind selects Elecsys Technologies to support operations and maintenance TGS 4C | 4C Offshore News
Baltic Wind selects Elecsys Technologies to support operations and maintenance
Elecsys Technologies has announced that Poland’s first offshore wind farm,
the 1.2GW Baltic Power project, has selected the company’s Safeguarding
Networks and Explorer platform to support its future operations and maintenance
activities.
The Baltic Power offshore wind farm is a joint venture between ORLEN and
Northland Power. The project comprises 76 wind turbines, each with a capacity
of 15MW, located approximately 23 kilometres offshore.
Under the agreement, Elecsys said its platform will incorporate Baltic
Power’s safety procedures and support high- and low-voltage operations
across the Choczewo onshore substation, offshore substations and the wind
farm’s 76 turbines.
“A safe system of work has to hold together from the onshore substation
to the furthest turbine, for every operator and every contractor on site.
Our job is to make sure the people doing that work have one clear, trusted
way of doing it, for every day the wind farm is in operation,” said Ryan
Murphy, chief executive of Elecsys.

title: VARD launches hull for UPO's offshore wind service vessel
content:
VARD has marked a milestone in the construction of the NB966 Commissioning
Service Operation Vessel (CSOV) for U-Ming Marine Offshore (UPO), with
the vessel's hull launched at the company's shipyard in Tulcea, Romania.
UPO is a joint venture between U-Ming Marine Transport Corporation and
World Marine Offshore A/S. The company provides logistics and transportation
services for offshore wind, power sector and other maritime projects.
According to VARD, the vessel will remain in Tulcea for the completion
of the remaining construction work before undergoing final outfitting,
commissioning and testing ahead of delivery, which is scheduled for the
second quarter of 2027.
The vessel is based on VARD's 4 19 design, a hybrid service operation vessel

Zelestra and Statkraft sign long-term tolling agreement for Italian battery storage project
Zelestra and Statkraft have signed an eight year physical tolling agreement
for a battery energy storage project in central Italy.
The agreement covers Zelestra's 175 MW, four hour battery energy storage
system (BESS), which will be connected to a Terna substation. The project
is expected to begin operations in 2028 and will be built and operated
Under the agreement, Statkraft will leverage its market access and battery

power markets."

now has 5.4 GWh of batteries under contract, with 3.5 GWh located in Italy
across four projects, which puts us firmly among the global leaders in
storage.
"As the regulated market advances with the second MACSE auction, a
bilateral market is developing in parallel, one that rewards solid, connection
ready projects."
The project is expected to support Italy's evolving energy storage market
while helping to improve renewable energy integration and energy security.

title: Turbine installation completed at 500MW Dieppe-Le Tréport offshore wind farm
content:
Ocean Winds has completed turbine installation at the 500MW Dieppe-Le
Tréport offshore
wind farm following a six month installation campaign that began in June.
Located off the Normandy coast, the project comprises 62 8MW wind turbines
installed on jacket foundations. Once fully operational, the wind farm
is expected to generate enough renewable electricity to power around 850,000
homes and businesses.
The project has been progressively generating renewable energy since first
power was achieved in July. With all turbines now installed, commissioning
activities will continue ahead of full commercial operation.
According to Ocean Winds, the project is expected to support around 3,500
jobs during its development and construction phases. The operation and
maintenance base in Dieppe will sustain approximately 70 long-term jobs
throughout the wind farm's 25 year operational life. In addition, the project
is expected to generate around €180 million of economic activity for small
and medium sized enterprises (SMEs).
Marc Hirt, Country Manager for France at Ocean Winds, said: "Completing
turbine installation at Dieppe-Le Tréport is an important milestone for
the project, but also for Ocean Winds in France. It demonstrates our ability
to deliver complex offshore wind projects and brings the wind farm another
step closer to full operation."
Frédéric Flaus, Project Director at Éoliennes en Mer Dieppe-Le Tréport,
added: "The installation of this final wind turbine marks the end
of more than ten years of development, consultation and collective effort.
It also follows several years of offshore works made possible by the commitment
and professionalism of all the project teams and partners."
The project is expected to support France's energy transition by increasing
domestic renewable energy generation, strengthening energy security and
delivering long term economic benefits to the Normandy region through jobs,
investment and local supply chain opportunities.

title: The Information’s 2026 Gift Guide
content: In a twisted version of future Christmases, perhaps AIs will carry out all the tasks involved in gift giving. But lucky for us, Andy Jassy still has all the bots blocked! So here once again is The Information’s annual Gift Guide, a project that we pursue with as much consideration and rigor as our everyday reporting. None of these items come via a publicist’s pitch, and none of the suggestions contain affiliate links. These are all things that we genuinely love and can picture wrapping up ourselves. Suffice it to say, there’s nothing artificial about our studious consideration and good taste. Entertainment I couldn’t afford most Nintendo 64 games growing up, so I was a frequent presence at the local video game rental store: I distinctly remember taking home the original version of “The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time”—and needing to return it jusstttt as I was on the cusp of saving Hyrule, the game’s fictional realm, and beating the big baddie, Ganondorf. This Switch 2 remake of the game has given me a shot at redemption. It’s one of the most critically lauded games of the year—and for good reason. The graphics are dazzling, and I can only describe them as “wet”: Everyone looks magnificently dewy. I also cannot overrecommend the nostalgia dopamine hit from getting to rummage through those treasure chests again.— Justin McCraw, senior software engineer A couple of weeks ago, the internet was abuzz about an AI-generated trailer that imagined an alt-history in which Nazi Germany and America wage some sort of temporal war. Sure, the clip was cool, but I still have my doubts about whether we’re yet at the point where AI can make a comprehensible feature film. In the meantime, there’s “Fatherland,” a 1992 alt-history bestseller from Robert Harris, the ultra-dependable thriller author. It imagines a 1960s landscape where Nazi Germany triumphed in Europe during World War II, and an aging Hitler clings to power. I think it’s Harris’ best world-building effort, which he accomplished through an enormous amount of research into how Hitler’s chief architect, Albert Speer, hoped to transform Berlin. (Those plans included the Volkshalle, a massive dome; in the novel, Harris supersizes Speer’s own ambitions, imagining the Volkshalle as a structure large enough to have its own microclimate.) “Fatherland” is taut as hell and completely unputdownable—with a weary, disillusioned city police captain, Xavier March, caught up in an intricate plot that runs through the Reich’s highest ranks. As March investigates, he keeps practically tripping over dead bodies. Then there’s the mystery of the terrible secrets kept in a hidden Swiss bank account.— Abram Brown, features editor Taking a photo with a physical camera keeps you in that moment you’re trying to capture in a way that a smartphone camera just doesn’t. Psych Blues sells camera film that has been pre-exposed, a process that imposes interesting colors and shapes onto the final prints—sorta like Instagram filters. The film comes in rolls or embedded in disposable 27-shot cameras. My husband and I had the cameras at our wedding, and they were a huge hit.— Christina Troitino, senior vice president, strategy and operations These books are basically a fancy paint-by-numbers setup for amateur watercolorists. They come in lots of fun seasonal patterns, and they’re an approachable lesson in how watercoloring actually works through mixing and shading. (I’m almost done with the dozen prints in the “Autumn” book, and I’ve already graduated to trying my hand at watercoloring without using a workbook.) Relaxing and no experience required!— Meredith Mazzilli, finance editor This historical fiction novel takes place in the 19th century, with Thomas Edison, Nikola Tesla and George Westinghouse waging war over the commercialization of electricity. It originally came out in 2016, but I found it an especially intriguing read as I considered how the AI era has ushered in another time of great technological change. As with AI, the advent of electricity had a dark side: Sure, homes got light bulbs, but then there was also the development of the electric chair.— Claire Harris, senior vice president, growth This Fender guitar amplifier is no bigger than a pack of cards: It’s small and light—just plug in headphones. It’s perfect for apartments and comes preinstalled with everything from fuzz pedals and droney loop effects to digital recreations of vintage gear. Since buying one, I’ve never played more.— Ryan Barwick, reporter On the banks of the Seine in Paris, Shakespeare and Company is an English-language indie bookstore known for supporting aspiring writers , and it offers its Year of Reading subscription service: three shipments of four books, many translated from French or connected to French culture, that arrive throughout the year. One recent selection was the 2024 English translation of “Like a Sky Inside,” which grew out of author Jakuta Alikavazovic’s experiences sleeping in the Louvre.— Amy Dockser Marcus, reporter For anyone who has caught the audiophile bug, this streaming device is a great way to bring high-fidelity music from services like Tidal, Spotify and Qobuz into a living room for use with a stereo amp and speakers.— Nick Wingfield, co-executive editor Gadgets I got hooked on the Govee TV Backlight—a strip of 60 LED lights that attach around a television—at a friend’s place. I was playing video games when I noticed the wall behind the TV changing color with the game. Explosions flashed orange. Dark scenes turned the room blue. It’s a simple but very effective setup. The lights come with a small camera that’s mounted to the TV’s front; it monitors the screen and guides the color changes. It’s fun with movies, too. Put on a horror film and the walls bleed red.— Qianer Liu, reporter When I use my Kindle Paperwhite, I sometimes think back to that classic line uttered by Dr. Otto Octavius in “Spider-Man 2”: “The power of the sun in the palm of my hand!” Admittedly, the Kindle Paperwhite will not aid anyone in a destructive bid for world domination. But it’s a marvelous, remarkably lightweight (7.4 ounces) device, and the one I have has stood the test of time. It’s been going strong for 10 years and has gotten me through everything from all seven Harry Potter books to this year’s “ How to Rule the World ” by Theo Baker. It became even more powerful when I discovered Libby, an app that lets me borrow and download ebooks from the New York Public Library. The latest Paperwhites come in some new pastel colors .— Zach Vallese, producer, TITV First, an apology. Last year, I also recommended a mechanical keyboard, the Lofree Flow84, that I thought hit a Goldilocks sweet spot: not too chunky, not too clicky. But as I learned myself over the past year, colleagues may not appreciate the delightful thock sound that emanates with each keystroke. To make full amends, allow me to introduce the IQUNIX MQ80, a mechanical keyboard that is just as much a dream to type on but produces a softer noise, like popping bubble wrap, that irritates desk neighbors far less. Also, it glows with rainbow lights. (Take note: the MQ80 is heavier than its compact size would suggest, so it’s meant to live on a desk, not travel on a commute.)— Rocket Drew, reporter As much as I love technology, I’ve lately found myself wanting less of it. Between endless social media scrolling and constantly checking notifications, my phone has become an endless hole. The problem is that I still need it for everyday things like sending texts, getting directions, listening to podcasts and paying for the subway. I wanted a way to access those essentials without carrying my phone around in my hand. That’s where I found the TinyPod. It’s a silicone case that turns your Apple Watch into something that resembles an old-school iPod. It comes in two versions: a standard model with a scroll wheel and the Lite model that’s just the case. (I opted for the Lite; sadly, it’s currently sold out.) I don’t have a cellular plan for my Apple Watch, so my iPhone still needs to be nearby. But out of sight, out of mind: I keep my phone buried at the bottom of my Patagonia Atom Sling Bag and keep the TinyPod in my pocket.— Z.V. These noise-canceling earbuds will help any poor sleeper drift off in comfort and not be woken up by noises during the night. They’re well designed and comfortable to wear in all sleeping positions. The package also comes with ear tips of various sizes and there’s definitely one that will fit your ears perfectly. . An accompanying app controls white noise levels, plays podcasts and sets a wake-up alarm. It also displays a neat amount of data on sleep duration, posture, surrounding noise and snoring. (It’s been such a comfort knowing I don’t snore after years of wondering about it.) My colleague Nick Wingfield previously recommended an earlier generation, the A20s. The A30s have active noise cancellation—just as Apple’s latest AirPods do—which uses tiny microphones to detect incoming sounds and speakers to emit sound waves that can cancel them out.— Jing Yang, Asia bureau chief My wife and I picked up one of these digital calendars a couple years ago, and it really lives up to the company’s pitch—keeping all our schedules and lists housed in one place. We put it up right next to the door to our garage, so we can easily take a quick glance before we take the kids to school and catch if anything moved on the schedule. With a click, we can see our grocery list and add more ketchup to it. (My daughter goes through about a bottle a day; she’s trying to cut down.) It syncs to our work Google Calendars and comes with a mobile app that allows us to add and keep track of changes when we’re not near the physical calendar. Initially, we were skeptics and expected to return it, but it really is a great product that helps keep our family of four organized.— Clark Miller, design director Like my colleague Zach Vallese, I’d been fantasizing about putting aside my smartphone on the weekends—a small act of rebellion in the age of social media and AI—but couldn’t fully bring myself to do it: I still wanted a device that could do some basic tasks, like helping me get from point A to point B. The Light Phone is a godsend. It has a smartphone’s basic features, including a map, but that’s it. (The latest edition, Light Phone III, adds a camera and is available for preorder with delivery expected in late December.)— Yueqi Yang, reporter Health and Wellness I love my SaunaBox—a portable home sauna at a reasonable price, which stands about as tall as a phone booth and goes up to 140 degrees Fahrenheit. It’s great to loosen sore muscles after a workout or just to relax after a stressful day before bed. I’m also convinced it kills or weakens colds. Plus, the latest models come with red light therapy for added benefits.— C.H. Koala Eco’s hand and body care products are scented with essential oils, not synthetic fragrances, so everything smells clean and fresh. The Naturalist box pairs rosalina, a soft lemony lavender, with crisp peppermint, so washing up and moisturizing feel like a little aromatherapy reset. It includes a hand wash, body wash and lotion, and the bottles are recyclable and refillable. It’s an everyday luxury.— Emily Ha, events production manager This body oil is nontoxic and clinically proven to improve skin hydration, increase skin radiance and reduce the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles. It comes in a gorgeous glass bottle that instantly makes a medicine cabinet look more chic, and the sandalwood scent is so dreamy it might just lull you to sleep.— Caryn Doyle, senior vice president, people I start every morning with Pilates by Sorel, an online pilates studio led by founder Sorel Carradine. It has a weekly schedule of curated sessions (streamed via smartphone or desktop) and a library that covers full-body workouts, multi-week programs and more. All you need is a mat, so it works at home, in a hotel room or in the 20 minutes between calls. (For anyone living or visiting Los Angeles, I’d also encourage taking an in-person at Carradine’s physical studio.) Pilates by Sorel also sells gift cards, which are an easy gift for anyone who keeps saying they’ll get back into a workout routine. —Lindsay Meech, chief advertising officer This lip balm has gone viral on TikTok, and I get why. It’s not sticky, looks good and actually lasts, a pretty rare trifecta as far as lip glosses go. It also has a fun metal applicator that’s easy to clean. My favorite shade is Sakura Shaved Ice, a sparkly light pink . — Alex Eichenstein, reporter I bought this for myself—and my mom immediately stole it. Red light supports skin appearance and surface-level recovery, while near-infrared light penetrates deeper to support muscle recovery and general well-being. Great for achy joints.— C.D. Home After hearing about Storyworth from a friend, I got it for my dad last year: It’s a service that sends a thought-provoking question to the person you’ve bought it for every week for a year via email or text. Then it compiles their answers into a physical book, which can also include pictures. The questions can be tailored, and admittedly, some are a little corny: What was your wedding like? What’s a small decision that changed your life? What advice would you give your 21-year-old self? For the first few weeks, my dad approached the assignment begrudgingly. In response to a question about what he would save from a home fire, he wrote: “my passport.” But as the weeks went on, his responses became longer and more reflective. Recently, he delivered copies of the finished book to me and my siblings, and well, I learned so much about him—I found reading about his life inspiring and beautiful. I now recommend Storyworth whenever I can: My dad says it’s his favorite gift he’s ever received.— Jemima McEvoy, reporter As a father of three boys, I’m constantly pumping something up—from every sports ball imaginable to the fleet of bikes in the garage. It used to be a very manual process … and take forever. But this portable air compressor makes the job easier, faster and, dare I say, fun. And now that my sons are a little bit older, they can handle it themselves.— Blake Boznanski, sales director When traveling, I keep a hit list of renowned coffee roasters to try and rate. Sometimes I’ll return from a trip with three or four bags of beans from different shops to brew later. One of my favorites that I’ve found is Kumquat Coffee in Los Angeles. If you know someone like me, I’m sure they’d love a subscription to Kumquat’s Coffee Club. Each month, Kumquat selects new beans from an international roaster and sends a bag to subscribers. What they’ve chosen so far matches some of the best cafes I’ve been to—from Copenhagen to Osaka. It also has a matcha subscription.— Shane Burke, senior data journalist As a slow drinker, I find it luxurious not to have to get up every 10 minutes to reheat my cup of ambition with this rechargeable mug, which keeps a drink warm through a temperature-controlling mobile app. I like it so much I now actually have one at home and one at the office. The newly released version, the Ember 3, is even dishwasher safe.— David Polk, senior product manager When my boyfriend wanted to spend $100 on a trash can, I admit I was skeptical. But I’ve been won over by this twin-bin one, which separates trash and recycling under the same lid. That lid is particularly nice—with beveled edges that allow it to close firmly and keep smells from seeping out. That means it can sit out in the open and not get shoved under the sink. It’s perfect for neatniks or anyone who has had a, uh, trash year.— Catherine Perloff, reporter The ceramic, nonstick surface on GreenPan’s items makes cooking and cleanup incredibly easy. It’s comforting to know the coating uses nontoxic and eco-friendly materials—and isn’t made using PFAS, long-lasting chemicals that have been linked to health risks.— Lin Gordon, vice president, acquisition Is this gadget an absurd appliance that takes up an inordinate amount of counter space? Yes. Will it spark joy with delicious—perhaps even healthy-ish—ice cream made with minimal effort? Also yes. The soft-serve version is a fun upgrade.— Leo Schwartz, reporter Kids and Toddlers Ever since Microsoft’s Kinect and Nintendo’s Wii Fit were discontinued, I’d been wanting to find a family-friendly gaming device that would encourage my kids to move around a little. The Nex Playground, a colorful, cube-shaped object, adds games constantly and is simpler to use than, say, Meta Platform’s Quest headsets. Right now, it has more than 60 games, many of which have options for more than two players. My crew loves some of the old-school titles, like Pac-Man and Hungry Hungry Hippos. Occasionally, I do the Zumba game, too.— C.H. Each month, subscribers receive a box of premeasured ingredients to make a yummy treat while learning about a STEM-focused theme. My kids get so excited when the box arrives, and it’s a wonderful way to spend quality time together on rainy or cold days. Upcoming kits include Melting Snowman Brownies (a lesson in how temperature works and how things freeze and melt) and Tornado Pretzel Twists (a lesson in, yes, tornadoes and vortex weather).— C.H. While the Camp Snap looks like it’s a disposable camera, it’s not. It’s a screenless digital camera meant to let kids enjoy the serendipity of photography without obsessing over the results and how they look in the shots. (The company’s founder got the idea for the product after looking around for cameras to send off with his kids to camp.) I like that it stops my kids from falling into the instant-gratification trap, and it’s a treat to later go through what they captured together. One charge lasts for 500 shots, and the camera has been sturdy enough to hold up with my 3-year-old using it.— L.M. These boxes of toys are a delight and cover a wide range of ages—from newborns to age 8. “The Looker” kit (birth to 12+ weeks) is heavy on high-contrast cards and mirrors, which work to improve visual acuity. Ones for slightly older kids (ages 3 to 4) focus on math and reading, with counting games and brightly colored letter blocks. All are meant to build problem-solving abilities; some focus on motor dexterity. (Bonus: They come with legible instructions and tips for parents to help encourage their kids to play with the toys.) On the younger end, they’re a great gift for new parents—one less thing for them to think about.— M.M. We’ve mainly used our SlumberPod when traveling with our baby (now toddler) and it has become a nonnegotiable for us: As in, we’re never leaving home without it. In a hotel or some other shared room with a little one, it’s a total game changer. It creates a completely dark space for them to sleep, while adults can keep the lights on, watch TV or enjoy a little time to themselves after bedtime. I also love that there’s ventilation and room for a fan, so it doesn’t feel stuffy.— Lauren Donovan, director of events I’ve tried at least 20 snack cups, and this is the first one where the lid stays on and a toddler can actually pull food in and out. It also comes with a suction cup for toddlers willing to stay in one place while eating. (What’s that like? I wouldn’t know.) Even better: Throw frozen veggies and a little bit of water in the cup, and it can go into the microwave to make mess-free steamed veggies. Scrambled eggs work, too. The MorePeas site has a ton of one-cup recipes , like fried rice, mini pancakes and a 90-second blueberry muffin. Frankly, I’d pay $200 for a snack cup if it got my toddler to actually eat; happily, this one is only $25.— Erin Weaver, vice president, audience development and strategy Every kid is going to want this thing, and I make that prediction confidently because I recently saw how much fun a friend’s child was having flying it around. (After much begging, my friend’s kid let me have a turn, too.) The drone is small, foldable and easy to fly with a controller that resembles a Wii remote. Just point it, and off the drone goes. (Many drones have much more complicated controllers that look more like portable gaming consoles.) It comes with a headset, and once it’s on, it immerses you in 360-degree, 8K video of the footage being captured by the drone. It’s like you’re looking through its eyes—and it sorta makes you feel like you’re flying. It can go for 24 minutes on a charge and climb to nearly 15,000 feet. Eventually, I did give the drone back to my friend’s kid. I admit it: The kid had to ask three times before I did.— Q.L. Wardrobe Normally, I’m not a handbag person—my keys, phone and wallet are usually just in my pockets. But when I saw a garnet-colored Petit Moyen, I knew I was meant to have it. I like how you can mix and match straps and accessories. Plus, it’s roomy, which means it’s a practical choice for toting around those daily essentials.— E.H. As someone who’s constantly trying—and failing—to cut back on my clothes shopping, I’ve been impressed with how BNTO has actually scratched my itch for purchasing new items every month. It’s a clothes-rental service, like Rent the Runway. But unlike other clothing-subscription services that cater to older folks or focus on dull professional clothing, BNTO is for women in their 20s who want items from smaller, more indie brands that offer trendier, contemporary clothing, like Damson Madder and Woodrose Deli. Each box contains six pieces, and subscribers have the opportunity to buy clothes they like at a heavily discounted price at month’s end.— Stephanie Palazzolo, reporter This Vancouver-based shoe company makes truly waterproof sneakers thanks to a high-tech breathable knit fabric it calls Dyma-Tex. They’re comfortable and machine washable, and I particularly like Vessi’s Weekend Classic line, which resembles old-school Reeboks and slip on and off like a pair of socks.— D.P. Barbour, the venerable British clothier, is a few seasons into a collab with FARM Rio, a Brazilian fashion brand known for its bold patterns, and their partnership has yielded some fun, whimsical reimaginings of heritage items. title: How cutting-edge prosthetics can help probe the human mind
content:
How cutting-edge prosthetics can help probe the human mind
Avi Davidson has volunteered to find out how a bionic hand that feels might alter his brain and nervous system.
Over the last few weeks, I’ve been talking to Alexander (Avi) Davidson. There are a lot of remarkable things about Avi. He sustained a horrific injury as a teenager, which left him paralyzed and without a left hand. Today, he uses his own experience to guide his practice as a trauma therapist.
He’s also taking part in a clinical trial of some new tech that allows him to move—and feel with—a prosthetic hand. Unlike standard prosthetics, this one connects directly to nerves in Avi's arm. He literally has wires coming out of his arm to plug it in with.
Avi’s the ninth person to trial this tech. But he’s the first to take it home and use it independently, for things like drinking from a cup (which is not easy) and writing (also not easy).
What struck me the most over our conversations was Avi’s outlook and approach to not just his injuries and learning to use this cutting-edge technology, but to life itself.
He has learned how to use something like seven different prosthetics in the 17 years since his accident. By taking part in this trial, he’s had to fit hundreds of hours of lab-based training and physical therapy around his demanding job. He had surgery to implant electrodes in his arm and will eventually need another to remove them. And he won’t even get to keep the latest prosthetic long term.
“While it’s unfortunate at times, and irritating at times, I do not regret what has come from [the accident], or the fact that it happened,” he told me. “I am not going to benefit from this … I wanted to be a part of this in the context of being able to help push the technology forward.”
The research team at the University of Utah that is running the trial hopes it will answer longstanding questions about the technology. How does it fare in a real-world setting, outside of the lab? What do people end up using it for? Where can improvements be made?
There may be some surprises along the way. Avi has found that his prosthetic wrist can feel sore and stiff when it’s been overused, just like his flesh-and-blood wrist. Weirdly, that feeling can be relieved by stretching it out. What’s going on here? No one really knows.
Scientists don’t know whether Avi’s brain will change as a result of using the bionic hand, either. Before the trial started, they performed brain scans to see how his missing left hand was represented in his brain. Will that change? And what might that mean for people who are born without limbs—how might a bionic limb affect their brains?
Avi will have the device until late January 2027 at the least, and potentially for another year. After that? Again, no one knows. It will depend on how the research is progressing, how Avi feels, and how much funding the team can secure. As a result, it’s not clear how long the device might even be expected to last in a person’s body.
I’ll be following this study, though, and will keep you posted.

title: Neuer Rekord bei BayernMentoring: 50 Tandems starten an der THWS
content:
Neuer Rekord bei BayernMentoring: 50 Tandems starten an der THWS
Frauen aus Hochschule und regionaler Wirtschaft begleiten als Mentorinnen MINT-Studentinnen
So viele Mentoring-Tandems wie nie zuvor: Für das Programmjahr 2026/27 haben sich für das BayernMentoring-Programm der Technischen Hochschule Würzburg-Schweinfurt (THWS) 50 MINT-Studentinnen (Mathematik, Informatik, Naturwissenschaft, Technik) und 36 Mentorinnen angemeldet.
Bei der Kick-off-Veranstaltung am Campus Ledward in Schweinfurt lernten sich viele der Tandems zum ersten Mal persönlich kennen. Ein Tandem besteht aus je einer Studentin und einer berufstätigen Frau im MINT-Bereich. Ein Jahr lang begleiten die berufserfahrenen Mentorinnen aus Unternehmen der Region die Studentinnen ehrenamtlich und unentgeltlich auf ihrem Weg ins Berufsleben. Ziel ist es, den Studentinnen Role Models zu zeigen, um sie zu einem erfolgreichen Studienabschluss zu ermutigen. Rollenbilder seien wichtig, um sich den eigenen Karriereweg vorstellen zu können, erklärt Anne-Kerstin Bartsch, Projektverantwortliche für BayernMentoring an der THWS.
Im vergangenen Jahr waren es 47 Tandems, schon damals hatte die THWS das größte BayernMentoring-Programm aller bayerischen Hochschulen. „Unsere Studentinnen sind fachlich hervorragend. Was ihnen oft fehlt, ist eine Frau, die sagt: ,Du schaffst das. Ich zeige dir, wie ich meinen Weg gegangen bin und unterstütze dich bei deinem'“, so Anne-Kerstin Bartsch. „Dass manche Mentorinnen sogar zwei Studentinnen begleiten, zeigt, wie viel Rückhalt es in unserer Region gibt. Ich bin den Mentorinnen unendlich dankbar für die Zeit und das Engagement, die sie in unsere Studentinnen investieren.“
Begrüßung, Matching und Impulse
Zum Auftakt begrüßten Anne-Kerstin Bartsch und Prof. Dr. Bettina Brandenstein-Köth, stellvertretende Frauenbeauftragte der THWS, die Teilnehmerinnen. Beide gaben Einblicke in ihre eigenen Erfahrungen und viele motivierende Impulse mit auf den Weg. Der Höhepunkt des Tages war das Matching: hier lernten sich die diesjährigen Tandems kennen. Moderatorin Nayomi Polcar führte durch den Tag und sprach in einem Impuls über Zukunftsängste und darüber, wie Verbindungen zu anderen Menschen dabei helfen können, diese zu überwinden.
Prof. Dr. Bettina Brandenstein-Köth, stellvertretende Frauenbeauftragte der THWS, stellt sich MINT-Studentinnen und deren Praxispartnerinnen vor (Foto: THWS/Anne-Kerstin Bartsch)
Ein individuelles Jahr
Was im Mentoring besprochen wird, bestimmen die Tandems selbst. Bei den Studierenden geht es zum Beispiel um den Berufseinstieg, die erste Bewerbung, um Karriereplanung, um das Gefühl, eine der wenigen Frauen im technischen Bereich zu sein, um Selbstvertrauen, Netzwerke oder die Fragen, wie sich Beruf und Familie vereinbaren lassen. Die Mentorinnen geben Einblick in ihren Arbeitsalltag in regionale Unternehmen und vermitteln Kontakt in die Praxis.
Frauen verbinden Frauen
Neben den Tandemtreffen bietet die THWS das ganze Jahr über Verschiedenes an, darunter eine STEM-Award-Verleihung (STEM steht im Englischen für Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics) gemeinsam mit dem Zonta Club Schweinfurt-Bad Kissingen im Dezember, eine Insight-Night unter dem Motto „Worüber sonst niemand spricht“, einen Selbstverteidigungskurs, Unternehmensbesuche, die THWS-Veranstaltung Science4Fem in Würzburg sowie weitere gemeinsame Termine. Gerade das macht das Programm aus: Es bringt Frauen aus Hochschule und Wirtschaft zusammen und schafft einen offenen Raum für Gespräche auf Augenhöhe.
„Viele Studentinnen merken hier zum ersten Mal: Mit meinen Fragen bin ich nicht allein“, erzählt Anne-Kerstin Bartsch. „Welchen Einfluss das Mentoring auf die Entwicklung unserer Studentinnen hat, wird am Anfang oft unterschätzt. Aus diesen Begegnungen entstehen Verbindungen, die oft weit über das Mentoringjahr hinaus bestehen und manchmal sogar zu lebensverändernden Entscheidungen führen. Die Mentorinnen sind Türöffnerinnen in die Arbeitswelt von morgen.“
Wichtig für die Hochschule und die Region
Für die THWS ist das Programm ein strategischer Baustein: Es stärkt Frauen in MINT-Fächern, hilft gegen den Fachkräftemangel in Mainfranken und verbindet die Hochschule eng mit der regionalen Wirtschaft. Unternehmen lernen früh gut ausgebildete Nachwuchskräfte kennen, Studentinnen bekommen einen direkten Draht in die Praxis.
Mentorin werden
Über BayernMentoring
BayernMentoring ist ein Programm der LaKoF Bayern, der Landeskonferenz der Frauen- und Gleichstellungsbeauftragen an bayerischen Hochschulen. Ziel ist die Gleichstellung von Frauen in Wissenschaft und Kunst. An der THWS richtet sich das Programm an MINT-Studentinnen ab dem dritten Bachelor- bzw. ersten Mastersemester und wird vom Büro der Frauenbeauftragten organisiert.
Mehr Informationen zu BayernMentoring
Über die THWS
Die Technische Hochschule Würzburg-Schweinfurt (THWS) zählt zu den größten Hochschulen für angewandte Wissenschaften in Bayern und steht seit ihrer Gründung im Jahr 1971 für hervorragende Lehre und angewandte Forschung. Mit rund 9.200 Studierenden, einem breit gefächerten Angebot von mehr als 60 Studiengängen sowie zwei Promotionszentren deckt die THWS ein weites Spektrum ab, das von Technik über Wirtschafts- und Sozialwissenschaften sowie Sprache bis hin zu Gestaltung reicht. Die THWS ist nicht nur regional in Franken und Bayern verwurzelt, sondern auch stark international ausgerichtet, was sich in zahlreichen Kooperationen und Austauschprogrammen weltweit und nicht zuletzt in einem vielseitigen englischsprachigen Studienangebot widerspiegelt.

Niclas Führling, Doktorand an der Constructor University, wurde auf der Konferenz IEEE ISAC 2026 in Lissabon (Portugal) mit dem „Best Student Paper Award“ ausgezeichnet.
| Quelle:
Niclas Führling
Download
Könnten die drahtlosen Netzwerke, die unsere Geräte miteinander verbinden, eines Tages autonomen Fahrzeugen und anderen Maschinen dabei helfen, ihre Umgebung wahrzunehmen und sich darin zurechtzufinden? Dies ist ein Kernziel der 6G-Funktechnologien und zugleich das Forschungsthema von Niclas Führling, Doktorand an der Constructor University, der auf der ersten IEEE-Konferenz zu integrierter Sensorik und Kommunikation (ISAC) den Preis für die beste studentische Arbeit gewann. Die Konferenz, die vom 15. bis 18. November in Lissabon, Portugal, stattfand, war die erste groß angelegte Veranstaltung, die sich dem Thema ISAC und seinen Anwendungen widmete.
Die ISAC-Technologie nutzt Funksignale nicht nur zur Kommunikation, sondern auch zur Umgebungserfassung, was bedeutet, dass sie Informationen über den Standort, die Entfernung und die Bewegung von Objekten liefern kann. Ihre Entwicklung ist Teil eines umfassenderen Bestrebens, das, was Forscher*innen als „Physical AI“ bezeichnen, zu entwickeln: Artificial Intelligence, die in der Lage ist, die physische Welt um sich herum wahrzunehmen und zu verstehen. Die Forschung von Führling und seinem Doktorvater, Professor of Electrical Engineering Guiseppe Abreu, konzentriert sich auf eine zentrale Herausforderung im Bereich ISAC: die Kalibrierung mehrerer Netzwerkstationen, damit diese zusammenarbeiten und Objekte in ihrer Umgebung präzise erkennen und verfolgen können.
„Stellen Sie sich vor, wie Hunderte von Menschen über eine belebte Kreuzung in der Stadt strömen können, ohne ständig miteinander zusammenzustoßen. Das ist eine angeborene Fähigkeit des Menschen und sogar einfacher Lebewesen, die für Roboter jedoch nach wie vor eine bemerkenswerte Herausforderung darstellt – selbst für solche, die mit hochentwickelten KI-Modellen arbeiten“, erklärt Prof. Abreu. „Die Herausforderung liegt nicht unbedingt in der Intelligenz im herkömmlichen Sinne, sondern in dem, was wir ‚physikalische Intelligenz‘ nennen: die Fähigkeit, unsere Umgebung in Echtzeit wahrzunehmen und darauf zu reagieren.“
Der Schlüssel zur Erschließung dieser Fähigkeit ist Präzision: Damit ISAC in dynamischen Umgebungen funktioniert, in denen eine momentane Lücke in der Wahrnehmung schwerwiegende Folgen haben könnte, müssen die Netzwerkstationen präzise synchronisiert sein. Selbst winzige Unterschiede im Timing und in der Frequenz eines Signals könnten die Fähigkeit des Systems beeinträchtigen, zwischen tatsächlichen Bewegungen in der Umgebung und durch die Geräte selbst verursachten Abweichungen zu unterscheiden.
Dies ist die Herausforderung, der sich Führling und seine Kolleg*innen in der preisgekrönten Arbeit „Joint Synchronization and Radar Parameter Estimation for OFDM-based DISAC Systems“ gestellt haben. Anstatt die Synchronisation als separate, vor der Objekterkennung zu lösende Voraufgabe zu betrachten, schlägt die Arbeit einen mathematischen Algorithmus vor, der es dem System ermöglicht, Synchronisationsunterschiede zwischen den Netzwerkstationen zu schätzen und gleichzeitig die Entfernung und Geschwindigkeit von Objekten zu ermitteln. Führling und seine Kolleg*innen führten Computersimulationen durch, um die Genauigkeit des Algorithmus im Vergleich zu etablierten Benchmarks nachzuweisen.
Für Führling bedeutet die Auszeichnung eine bedeutende Bestätigung sowohl für ihn persönlich als auch für die Arbeit der Forschungsgruppe „Communication and Sigtnal Processing“ der Constructor University. „Der ‚Best Student Paper Award‘ war für mich und unsere gesamte Forschungsgruppe eine unerwartete und große Ehre“, sagt er.
„Wir sind dem IEEE als weltweit größter Fachorganisation für Technik dankbar, dass es eine Konferenz organisiert hat, die sich ganz dem Thema ISAC widmet. Die Anzahl und das Kaliber der führenden Forscher*innen, die an dieser Eröffnungsveranstaltung teilgenommen haben, zeigen, wie wichtig das Thema für unser Fachgebiet ist, und unterstreichen die Bedeutung der Auszeichnung.“
Besuchen Sie die Webseite der School of Computer Science and Engineering der Constructor University, um mehr über unsere Forschungs- und Studienprogramme zu erfahren.

Prof. Dr.-Ing. Wenke Weinreich, Institutsleiterin am Fraunhofer-Institut für Photonische Mikrosysteme IPMS, ist in das neue Präsidium von Silicon Saxony gewählt worden.
